## Summary

Did 2.4 and then 3.1 in the same session. 2.4 is the permission surface (D8): recorded in run_started.surface, its settings file written per session and read back before every spawn, mode on --permission-mode where no settings source can outrank it, default acceptEdits plus a protocol-floor allow-list. 3.1 is the codex adapter, and the point of it is that codex fits the contract BADLY — four capabilities false where Claude Code has all six. Usage arrives only with turn.completed, which is after the session has ended, so usage() returns undefined forever and the threshold policy is refused rather than run on a post-mortem; no channel exists into a running exec; codex speaks a sandbox enum instead of per-tool rules; nothing reports cost. Two new capabilities, permission_rules and cost, carry the last two, and inertOptions makes the driver SAY what an operator's flag cannot do before the run starts (D9) — a recorded allow-list that had no effect and a cost cap that cannot fire are both silent traps. The session id is assigned rather than observed, since codex runs no sofar hook, and resolveLaunchedSession still believes it only because the record registered it, so D3 is exercised for real for the first time. Codex has no sofar MCP server either, so the pin line hands over the CLI dialect — and writing that surfaced a bug the drive-level test caught: task_status_changed takes `id`, not `task_id`, and a session told otherwise does the work and stalls silently. Shapes verified against the real codex-cli 0.136.0 at zero API cost by pointing it at an unreachable provider (promoted to repo memory); the same trick confirmed it accepts every flag the adapter builds. 1829 tests pass. Phase 2 is closed; Phase 3 is half done.

## Next action

Do 3.2: per-task routing — model and effort hints on a task, and the driver picking the adapter per task. Two things 3.1 leaves ready for it: DriveOptions already prefers the surface's model/effort over the flags, so per-task hints have to decide whether they beat the run's recorded surface or lose to it (they should lose, or a resumed run is not one run); and AGENTS in cli/drive.ts is now the only place that knows adapter names, so per-task adapter selection belongs there rather than in the loop. Note also that the codex pin line duplicates renderPrompt's protocol paragraph in CLI-dialect form — if a third adapter needs the same, that translation wants to move out of the adapter.
